newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Early Taiwan dlr slips amid active U.S. dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Early Taiwan dlr slips amid active U.S. dlr demand.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar slipped against the U.S. dollar in early Friday trade, but dealers said the central bank continued to sell U.S. dollars to prevent local unit's further slide.
After 30 minutes at 0130 GMT, the local unit was at T$28.727 against Thursday's T$28.725 close.
Turnover through dealers was active at US$70 million.
"U.S. dollar demand remains heavy, but the central bank is actively selling U.S. dollars to prevent the Taiwan dollar from falling below T$28.727 level," said one dealer.
Dealers said the Taiwan dollar faced depreciation pressure due to importers's strong greenback demand.
"Importers are afraid the Taiwan dollar will continue to fall, while exporters want to withhold their U.S. dollar position in hopes for a bigger gain," the dealer said.
"The central bank becomes the only (U.S. dollar) seller in the market," the dealer said.
A stable range of T$28.68-73 was seen for Friday.
